methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Uptool operates in Robotics & Manufacturing at an undisclosed stage. The addressable peer universe comprises 10 same-sector companies: 1 public entity (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private firms, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median method is inapplicable to this valuation. While 10 same-sector peers exist, stage and valuation-tier filtering yielded fewer than three datapoints in any cohort. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given sector-specific capital intensity and commercialization timelines in robotics. No same-stage comparable, adjacent-stage comparable, or similar-tier comparable subset reached the three-company minimum required for robust triangulation.

Without sufficient narrow-peer clustering, this analysis cannot support a quantitative valuation range anchored to multiples or median methods. The composition of the comp set—dominated by early-stage and growth-stage robotics ventures—suggests frameworks emphasizing cash-burn runway, technical risk reduction, and market traction would be more informative than conventional EV multiples. Any valuation recommendation would require: (i) disclosure of Uptool's actual stage and recent financing data, (ii) disclosure of comparable round size and investor composition from the top private peers listed, or (iii) application of venture method or scenario-based cash flow analysis contingent on product-market fit milestones. Current data insufficiency precludes defensible quantitative synthesis.
